evals.name: static-review-flawed-skill
evals.prompt: review skills/deploying-previews before I publish it. report only, don't edit anything
evals.expected_output: A static review report in the rubric format with severity-rated findings and locations: name/directory mismatch and client-specific frontmatter (critical), vague description, background padding, shouted rules, platform menu, vendor tool names and plugin variable, missing evals. Verdict 'major revision'. No files modified.
assertions: The report flags the name/directory mismatch as critical
The report flags the client-specific frontmatter fields (allowed-tools, disable-model-invocation, when_to_use)
The report flags the vague description 'helps with deployments'
The report flags vendor-specific tool names or the CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT variable in the body
The verdict is major revision (or equivalent: not publishable)

evals.name: interpret-flat-benchmark
evals.prompt: here's my benchmark for the commit-messages skill (benchmark.json in this folder). with_skill and without_skill are basically identical. is the skill useless?
evals.expected_output: Reads benchmark.json; notes that most assertions pass in both configs (non-discriminating) so the benchmark cannot show value; identifies the one assertion that differs; recommends replacing pass_both assertions with harder discriminating ones and adding cases where the baseline fails; notes the skill costs extra tokens; does not conclude 'useless' from this evidence alone.
assertions: The response explains that assertions passing in both configurations cannot measure the skill's value
The response names the assertion(s) that do differ between configurations
The response recommends adding harder or more discriminating assertions or cases rather than concluding the skill is useless
The response mentions the token or time cost delta

evals.name: write-trigger-queries
evals.prompt: write the trigger eval queries for skills/writing-adrs so we can tune its description. put them where the eval scripts expect them
evals.expected_output: skills/writing-adrs/evals/trigger-queries.json with ~20 realistic queries, roughly balanced, should-trigger including implicit cases (a change that adds a datastore without mentioning ADRs), should-not-trigger near-misses (README, changelog, design doc, reviewing an ADR), valid JSON per schema.

assertions.text: trigger-queries.json exists, is valid, has 16-24 queries with at least 7 of each label

assertions: At least two should-trigger queries never mention ADRs or decision records explicitly
Most should-not-trigger queries are near-misses involving documentation or decisions rather than unrelated topics
